summary: This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to eliminate the Optional Practical Training Program, prohibiting work authorization for foreign students on F-1 visas who are no longer in full-time study unless authorized by a new act of Congress.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to eliminate the Optional Practical Training (OPT) program, which provides work authorization to F-1 student visa holders. There is no mention of government spending, budgets, appropriations, or fiscal impacts. It solely addresses immigration employment authorization rules. No bearing on government spending.

The bill focuses exclusively on prohibiting employment authorization under the OPT program for nonimmigrant students. No provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue. No relation to taxation.
No references to healthcare, insurance, medical services, or public/private health systems. The bill is strictly about immigration work authorization for students.
The bill does not mention firearms, Second Amendment, regulations, or rights. Entirely unrelated to gun control.

The bill's core purpose is to eliminate the OPT program, which allows foreign students (F-1 visa holders) to work in the US post-graduation, a key pathway for high-skilled immigration. Titled 'Fairness for High-Skilled Americans Act,' it explicitly prioritizes American workers by restricting this immigration-related work authorization without new congressional approval. This directly restricts immigration pathways and protections for foreign workers/students, aligning strongly with the +1 direction (restrict immigration and enforce borders). The entire bill is about this change, making it primarily focused on immigration restriction.
No mention of abortion, reproductive rights, or related issues. Unrelated.
No provisions on military, defense, or spending in those areas. Bill is about civilian immigration policy.
No environmental regulations, climate policies, or protections discussed. Unrelated.
No references to welfare, food stamps, or safety net programs. Focus is on employment authorization for immigrants.

The OPT program applies to F-1 students post-graduation, but the bill targets work authorization, not education funding, curriculum, school choice, or federal involvement in education. It does not engage with education policy directly.
No drug-related provisions, enforcement, or decriminalization. Unrelated.
Bill does not address sentencing, policing, reform, or justice system. It's an immigration employment rule.
No trade agreements, tariffs, free trade, or protectionism. Unrelated to trade.
No discussion of debt, deficits, or fiscal policy. No spending or revenue changes specified.
No LGBTQ+ protections, discriminations, or related rights. Unrelated.
No foreign aid provisions. Bill is domestic immigration policy.
No voting access, elections, or integrity measures. Unrelated.
No tech regulations, data privacy, or oversight. Unrelated.

While eliminating OPT reduces foreign labor competition, potentially benefiting American workers, the bill does not engage with labor laws, unions, worker protections, or employer flexibility directly. It is framed as immigration policy for 'high-skilled Americans,' not labor/union policy. No genuine engagement with labor/unions topic.
No religious exemptions, civil rights, or discrimination issues. Unrelated.
